ssrf_posture_from_code.pre_flight: ValidateURL: http/https only, no embedded credentials, host required, and a LITERAL non-public IP refused. Hostnames are deliberately NOT resolved here.
ssrf_posture_from_code.real_guard: net.Dialer.Control runs after DNS resolution, once per candidate IP — this is what defeats DNS rebinding and what covers redirect hops.
ssrf_posture_from_code.redirects: CheckRedirect re-validates each target with ValidateURL and caps the chain at 5 (maxRedirects).
ssrf_posture_from_code.proxy: http.Transport.Proxy is nil — HTTP(S)_PROXY cannot route around the dialer.
ssrf_posture_from_code.relax_key: HTTP_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS -> config.ImportAllowPrivateURLs (config.go ~576), default false, feeding videoimport.WithAllowPrivateFetch AND channelsync.WithAllowPrivateURLs. validate() REFUSES to boot production with it set; a development boot logs 'URL-import SSRF guard RELAXED ... NEVER enable this in production'. Its absence from the phase-1 logs is how that phase is known to have run with the guard intact.

defects_found_and_fixed.id: ytdlp height cap excluded unknown-height formats
defects_found_and_fixed.measured: yt-dlp --list-formats on the fixture watch page reports one format: '0 mp4 unknown | http | unknown unknown'. With the SHIPPED default YTDLP_MAX_HEIGHT=1080 the selector 'height<=1080' matched nothing, yt-dlp exited 'Requested format is not available', and resolver=ytdlp dead-lettered as 'the URL could not be imported from this platform'. The same page downloads clean with height<=?1080 (h264 + aac) and with the uncapped selector.
defects_found_and_fixed.why_it_matters: the case the selector's own comment is written for — a PeerTube static web video, whose codecs it documents as UNKNOWN — reports an unknown height for the same reason. YTDLP_MAX_HEIGHT=0 was the only working configuration.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: every height comparison carries yt-dlp's '?' operator; the cap still binds every format that declares a height.

defects_found_and_fixed.id: resolver=auto fell through to the unpinned extractor on an address the guard refused
defects_found_and_fixed.measured: an import of a public-hostname URL that 302s to 127.0.0.1 was accepted 202, the guarded HEAD was refused, the job resolved to ytdlp, and the extractor followed the redirect and downloaded the loopback file (state done, bytes stored).
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: probeContentType now reports the guard's refusal to the caller and probeAuto stops instead of falling back. BOTH sentinels count: ErrBlockedAddress from the dial-time control hook, and ErrInvalidURL from CheckRedirect re-validating a hop — the path a LITERAL private address in a Location header takes, which the first cut of the fix missed and the re-measurement caught. A 405, a timeout, a TLS error or a redirect loop still fall back, so no legitimate platform URL regresses. An explicit resolver=ytdlp is untouched.

defects_found_and_fixed.id: imports_enabled did not stop channel auto-sync
defects_found_and_fixed.measured: with URL import off instance-wide (POST /videos/{id}/import 403, features.imports and features.import_http false), /instance still advertised channel_sync=true, POST /channel-syncs answered 201 and sync-now 202. The sync worker enqueues through videoimport.Enqueue, BELOW the handler that 403s, so the operator's master switch left a worker importing third-party uploads on a timer.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the master clause is folded into both the HTTP gate (httpapi.channelSyncEnabled) and the per-tick predicate (cmd/api's channelsync.WithEnabledFunc).
defects_found_and_fixed.post_fix_measurement: with imports_enabled=false a sync forced due at 08:55:28 had NOT run 95 seconds later (last_sync_at frozen at 08:53:48); with it back on the same forced run fired at 08:57:48. In Chromium the Studio auto-sync section shows its disabled state while imports are off.

findings_recorded_not_fixed: The three boot-capability 503s (resolver=ytdlp, channel-sync create, sync-now) are bare echo.NewHTTPError, so the 5xx scrubber replaces their sentences with 'an unexpected error occurred'. A17's open item; the typed-error idiom that fixes it already ships next door as live_not_configured / mail_not_configured.

URL import has a hard 60-second budget for the WHOLE download: videoimport.fetchTimeout is passed as http.Client.Timeout, which bounds the body read. The effective ceiling is 60 seconds of the origin's throughput, not UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE (5 GiB by default), and there is no knob. Needs a configuration surface and a product ruling.
A failed channel sync has no backoff — it reschedules at the plain CHANNEL_SYNC_INTERVAL forever, so a permanently dead source is re-listed at full rate indefinitely.
channel_syncs is still unprojected into job_runs and still has no admin surface; this slice added only a WARN line.
A runtime limit change binds the worker only after its settings-poll interval, so a just-lowered cap does not necessarily apply to the next job.
The channel-sync dedupe key falls back to the entry URL when the extractor reports no id; a source with unstable URLs and no ids would re-import.

The explicit resolver=ytdlp path is still not dial-pinned, by design — the documented residual risk that the off-by-default flag and YTDLP_PROXY exist to address. This slice closed only the AUTOMATIC route into it.
attempts_and_corrections: A tool-call timeout killed the fixture origin's process group mid-outage-test, so a 'recovery' that never came was the harness, not the product. The origin now starts under nohup ... & disown, and the sync recovered on the first run after a real restart.
The first cut of the SSRF fix matched only ErrBlockedAddress and let the literal-IP redirect through; re-measuring the case rather than assuming it fixed is what caught it.
A polling script read import_job['stage'], which is omitempty, and threw KeyError for two minutes against a healthy job.
Several actors' 15-minute access tokens expired mid-phase, turning real 202s into confusing 401s until every phase started with a fresh login.
upload_max_size_bytes=20000 was refused 422 by the settings validator (the floor is 1 MiB), so a >1 MiB fixture clip had to be generated before the size cap could be exercised at all.
